summary: The Thailand International Postgraduate Programme (TIPP) is a scholarship framework of the Thailand International Cooperation Agency (TICA), part of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Thailand, running since 2000 for people from developing countries. Candidates are nominated by their government. The 2026 round offers 22 courses at Thai universities: 21 master's programmes and one diploma, in six themes such as agriculture and food security, health and wellness, climate resilience, and trade and economy. The award covers tuition, insurance, allowances for living, accommodation, settlement, books and thesis, and in some cases airfare.
eligibility_notes:
Candidates must be nominated by the National Focal Point for International Development Cooperation (for example the foreign ministry) of a country or territory on the TIPP eligible list, or by the central government agency where they work. Each country or territory can nominate up to three candidates per academic programme.

Candidates should preferably work in the government sector or in the field of the course. They need a bachelor's degree and/or professional experience in a related field, and good English. If English is not their first language and their bachelor's was not taught in English, they must pass an English test under the university's rules. Other conditions follow the university's own regulations.

Candidates must be in good physical and mental condition and must not be pregnant.

The forms must be completed in English and endorsed by the candidate's supervisor and the National Focal Point.

Selection looks closely at the candidate's background, current government position, and the expected use of the knowledge on return, with attention to geographic spread and gender balance. Full-support countries are: Indonesia, Lao PDR, Malaysia, Myanmar, Philippines, Timor-Leste, Vietnam, China, Mongolia, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Nepal, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Jordan, Iraq, Palestine (West Bank and Gaza Strip), Iran, Lebanon, Kyrgyz Republic, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, Algeria, Egypt, Djibouti, Eritrea, Morocco, Mauritania, Tunisia, Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Comoros, DR Congo, Burundi, Rwanda, South Sudan, Ethiopia, Somalia, South Africa, Zimbabwe, Lesotho, Angola, Zambia, Botswana, Namibia, Eswatini, Malawi, Madagascar, Senegal, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Mali, Gambia, Cote d'Ivoire, Sierra Leone, Togo, Burkina Faso, Gabon, Cabo Verde, Liberia, Niger, Nigeria, Benin, Cameroon, Ghana, Central African (as printed), Congo, Equatorial Guinea, Sao Tome and Principe, Chad, Mozambique, Armenia, Moldova, Ukraine, Kosovo, Azerbaijan, Jamaica, Guatemala, Honduras, Nicaragua, Belize, Haiti, Peru, Venezuela, Colombia, Bolivia, Ecuador, El Salvador, Suriname, Paraguay, Papua New Guinea, Vanuatu, Solomon Islands, Fiji, Kiribati, Tonga, Samoa, Tuvalu, Micronesia, Tokelau. Partial-support countries are: Maldives, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Mauritius, Saint Helena, Belarus, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro, Albania, Turkiye, Georgia, North Macedonia, Serbia, Montserrat, Grenada, Dominican Republic, Dominica, Saint Lucia, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, Mexico, Cuba, Costa Rica, Panama, Brazil, Guyana, Argentina, Nauru, Niue, Marshall Islands, Palau, Wallis and Futuna. Countries on neither list can apply if they are on the general TIPP eligible list, but then the scholarship covers tuition only; that general list was not found.
age_experience_notes: No more than 45 years of age. A bachelor's degree and/or professional experience in a related field is needed; some courses add their own rules, for example Walailak's Health, Environment and Safety course asks for a GPAX of at least 2.75 or 3 years of related work.
funding_summary: TICA pays the tuition fee (not the equipment insurance fee, transcript and certificate fee), accident and hospitalisation insurance, a living allowance of 7,000 baht per month, an accommodation allowance of 7,000 or 9,000 baht per month, a 6,000 baht settlement allowance on first arrival, a books allowance of 10,000 baht per year (4 semesters for a master's), and a thesis allowance. Round-trip economy airfare is covered only for awardees from full-support countries. The courses run 1 or 2 years.
programmes_note: The 2026 list has 22 courses in six themes: Sufficiency Economy Philosophy for the SDGs; Agriculture and Food Security; Climate Resilience; Health and Wellness; Trade and Economy; Inclusive Development. Most are 2 years; Mahidol's Master of Primary Health Care Management and the Institute of Dermatology diploma are 1 year. The overview page names a seventh theme, Science, Technology and Innovation for Development, which has no course in the 2026 list. The TICA page does not state the teaching language; many course titles say International Program. Awardees must study full time and may not change the programme topic or study plan.
institutions_note: Thirteen Thai institutions host the 22 courses: Chiang Mai Rajabhat University, King Mongkut's University of Technology Thonburi, Maejo University, Chiang Mai University, Kasetsart University (Kamphaeng Saen campus), Walailak University, Mahidol University, Naresuan University, Mahasarakham University, Chulalongkorn University, the Institute of Dermatology, Prince of Songkla University and Rangsit University. Each university's own admission rules also apply.

benefits.limit_text: Tuition fee, reimbursed directly by TICA, except the equipment insurance fee and the transcript and certificate fee
benefits.conditions: Where the awardee's country is on neither the full-support nor the partial-support list, the scholarship covers tuition only.

benefits.limit_text: Living allowance of 7,000 baht per month
benefits.conditions: Paid monthly during study in Thailand.

benefits.limit_text: Accommodation allowance of 7,000 or 9,000 baht per month
benefits.conditions: The rate that applies is not explained. Awardees should bring about USD 300 for a rental deposit (usually 2 months) and the first month's rent; the deposit is returned when the contract ends.

benefits.limit_text: Round-trip economy airfare from the home country to Bangkok, plus domestic travel in Thailand to the university city; airport transfer
benefits.conditions: Airfare is paid for awardees from full-support countries only; partial-support countries pay their own airfare and travel costs. TICA books all tickets; extra baggage and home-country domestic travel are not covered.

benefits.limit_text: Accident and hospitalisation insurance during study
benefits.conditions: Pre-existing illness, dental treatment, brain disease, mental illness, pregnancy and glasses are not covered. Awardees are advised to buy their own travel insurance for lost or stolen belongings.

benefits.limit_text: Settlement allowance of 6,000 baht on first arrival; books allowance of 10,000 baht per year (4 semesters for a master's)
Thesis allowance: up to 20,000 baht for compulsory fieldwork or data collection, plus 12,000 baht for thesis printing or 8,000 baht for independent study printing
benefits.conditions: Fieldwork money needs expense details and TICA approval case by case.

The guidelines are not consistent: one list says TICA pays the visa fee for full-support countries, while the visa section says awardees pay all visa costs (visa fee, travel to the embassy, postage, transit visa).

requirements.text: TIPP application form, one original plus two copies, filled in English and endorsed by the candidate's supervisor and the National Focal Point. Also filled in online.
TICA medical report form (other health certificates are not accepted; an application without it is not considered).
Transcript of the bachelor's degree showing the courses taken.
Recommendation letters from at least 3 persons, one letter per person (for example a university teacher, supervisor or employer).
English test score (for example TOEFL or IELTS) as the university requires, not more than 2 years old at admission.
requirements.conditional_rule: Required of all; the university sets the minimum score

requirements.text: Other documents the university asks for, listed under the 'Document Required' heading of each course sheet (for example CV, research proposal, photographs, passport copy, health certificates). All documents must be in English.

application_steps.title: Check that your country can nominate and pick a course
application_steps.detail: Your government's National Focal Point must nominate you (the ministry of foreign affairs, or the central agency where you work). Each country or territory can nominate up to three candidates per programme. Choose one of the 22 courses and read its course sheet for the documents it needs.

application_steps.title: Fill in the online application form and prepare the documents
application_steps.detail: Complete the online form on the TICA site and prepare one original and two copies of each document: application form, TICA medical report, bachelor's transcript and certificate, at least 3 recommendation letters, an English test score and any extra documents the course asks for. Items 1 to 6 are mandatory. Everything must be in English and endorsed by your supervisor and the National Focal Point.

application_steps.title: Hand in the hard copy through the Royal Thai Embassy
application_steps.detail: The National Focal Point forwards the papers to the Royal Thai Embassy, Permanent Mission or Consulate-General for your country. The application is complete only when TICA has the hard copy. For 2026 the guidelines asked for papers to reach the embassy by 23 February 2026; this date has passed.

application_steps.title: TICA reviews nominations
application_steps.detail: TICA looks at each candidate's background, current government position, and how they plan to use the knowledge after returning. It also balances countries and gender, unless priority is set for certain countries or cooperation frameworks.

application_steps.title: University admission rules apply
application_steps.detail: Candidates also meet the host university's rules, including its English test when English is not their first language and their bachelor's was not taught in English. The sheets for some courses name extra papers, such as a research proposal or health certificates. The guidelines do not state when results are announced.

application_steps.title: Arrange travel and the Thai visa
application_steps.detail: Awardees must get a Non-immigrant visa Type F before travelling; TICA helps with the embassy and advice on papers. TICA books and changes the e-ticket for those on the full-support list, and an airport transfer is provided on arrival. Visa costs are discussed under benefits.

application_steps.title: Study full time under the conditions of the award
application_steps.detail: Awardees study full time and may not change the programme topic or study plan. Part-time work is not allowed and family members may not stay with them. An awardee who becomes pregnant in a way that stops attendance may lose the scholarship. TICA can withdraw the award if rules are broken.
